title: Caesar in Gaul
objective: After this level you can describe Caesar’s conquest of Gaul and why it made him so powerful.
summary: From 58 to 50 BCE Caesar conquered Gaul, beat Vercingetorix at Alesia, raided Britain, and gained wealth and a loyal veteran army.

cards.headline: Caesar spent eight years conquering Gaul, and wrote the history of it himself.
The conquest
cards.body: Between 58 and 50 BCE, Julius Caesar conquered Gaul, roughly modern France and Belgium. At Alesia in 52 BCE he defeated the Gallic leader Vercingetorix. He also led two expeditions to Britain, in 55 and 54 BCE.

cards.headline: Wealth, an army and a story
cards.body: The conquest gave Caesar enormous wealth and a veteran army loyal to him. He also wrote his own account, the Commentaries on the Gallic War, describing himself in the third person. Readers in Rome learned the war from Caesar’s point of view.

cards.fact: Caesar wrote about himself in the third person.
cards.context: His Commentaries on the Gallic War read as if an observer were describing Caesar’s deeds, which made his own story look like plain history.

cards.headline: Gaul: conquered
learned: He won wealth and a loyal army

questions.prompt: Whom did Caesar defeat at Alesia in 52 BCE?
questions.explanation: At Alesia, Caesar defeated the Gallic leader Vercingetorix.

questions.prompt: Why did the conquest of Gaul make Caesar dangerous to the Senate?

options.label: It gave him wealth and an army loyal to him
It made him king of the Gauls
It turned the Gauls against Pompey
options.rationale: The danger was Caesar’s own power.

questions.explanation: A rich general with devoted veterans could defy the Senate.

questions.prompt: From Level 32: why would Caesar’s veterans follow him rather than the Senate?

options.label: They were paid in Gallic gold by law
Generals, not the Senate, secured their pay and land
The Senate had disbanded the legions
They had sworn oaths to Vercingetorix

questions.explanation: Since Marius, soldiers looked to their commander for their pay and retirement land.
